success_patterns: Missing mandatory args with no cache key: output only a short seek_information. Examples: a flight request with an airport habit ('I normally fly from LEX') but no date, and a hotel budget reply with no check-in/check-out dates.

Round-trip date reply ('May 15, 2025 to May 19, 2025') becomes two assigned and saved search_flights calls with origin and destination taken from earlier turns, and no hotel or other domain added when none was requested.

Budget-only or rating-plus-budget replies on a cached restaurants key become a restaurant-only filter. They pass only the last turn's values (budget=30; rating=[4.5, 5], budget=40), with no re-passed cuisine or city.
First hotel search after restaurants are already cached carries every stated constraint (city, dates, stars, neighborhood) and leaves the restaurants key untouched.
Descriptors with no tool parameter ('business lunch', 'great view') are dropped. Only city and cuisine reach the restaurant search.

One miss that still passed: an airport code stated in an earlier turn ('I normally fly from SJC') was not carried into the later round-trip search. Gold adds start_airport on the outbound leg and end_airport on the return leg.

patch.reasoning: Nearly every observed success is already covered by the CACHE GATE, Rule 6, Rule 9 and the slow-update guidance, so I propose no new rules. The one gap is that Rule 9's date-reply bullet says 'Add no other params', which can suppress an airport code the user named in an earlier turn. Gold carries that code as start_airport and end_airport on the two legs. The edit pairs the prohibition with its positive trigger and does not add a new example.

edits.target: Add no other params: no airline, flight_class, budget, times or num_people.
edits.content: Carry an airport code the user named in ANY earlier turn ('I normally fly from SJC'): start_airport="SJC" on the outbound leg and end_airport="SJC" on the return leg, even when this turn only gives dates. Add no other params: no airline, flight_class, budget, times or num_people.
